title: [Update] You guys tore apart our local 2D-to-3D pipeline, so we spent the weekend rebuilding it. Jupetar V1.5 is now live.
author: Blackie-Chan101
selftext:
​Hey r/aigamedev,


​A few days ago I posted about Jupetar, the local, offline 2D-to-3D engine my co-dev and I built to escape cloud SaaS subscriptions and API paywalls. The response here was absolutely insane.


​The feedback, the brutal critiques on the textures, and the workflow suggestions were exactly what we needed. We were honestly blown away that so many of you understood exactly what we are trying to build—and a huge thank you to the devs who actually went ahead and picked up a copy to support the project.


​Our original plan was to take all your feedback, go heads-down for a few months, and eventually surface with V2.0. But after reading through the comments (especially regarding the VRAM spikes and the texture quality gap compared to cloud tools), we realized we couldn't leave V1.0 sitting as it was.


​So, we ripped the engine down to the studs and rebuilt the pipeline. Jupetar V1.5 is now live.
​Here is what we fixed based directly on your feedback:


​The "Wet Plastic" Chrome Bug is Dead
A few of you noticed the GLB exports looked way too shiny in standard viewers. We built a custom channel packer that strictly enforces glTF 2.0 ORM standards (packing Ambient Occlusion, Roughness, and Metallic data correctly into the right channels). Your assets will now natively render with a clean, matte finish in Unity, Unreal, and Blender.

​True 4K Neural Upscaling
The base AI textures from the V1 pipeline were a bit blurry. We stripped out the standard mathematical upscalers and wired the Real-ESRGAN x4plus neural network directly into Phase 3 of our pipeline to hallucinate and restore high-frequency micro-details.


​Dynamic Poly-Counts & The "Fast Path"
You asked for topology control. We added a Target Poly-Count slider to the UI (Low, Medium, High). We also added a dynamic "Fast-Path"—if you select Low or Medium for a quick blockout, the engine automatically bypasses the heavy neural upscaler to save VRAM and time, shaving massive amounts of compute off the generation.


​The "Monolith" Background Wall
We fixed the ingestion bug where the AI would sometimes extrude the background into a giant flat plane behind your character by overhauling how the engine interprets alpha and white-space.


​VRAM Telemetry & UI Polish
We added a live VRAM monitor graph directly into the UI so you can watch exactly how the engine manages your GPU memory spikes during the heavy texturing phase. We also added drag-and-drop input, decoupled the export formats (GLB, OBJ, PLY), and completely killed the backend terminal spam.


​What's Next for V2.0?
This patch stabilizes the foundation. Now we are officially moving onto V2.0. We are actively researching Trellis fast-path integration for rapid prototyping, Hunyuan 3.0 weights, and some serious, deep-level hardware optimizations to fundamentally drop the VRAM requirements.
​The free Demo on Steam has been updated with all the V1.5 architecture so you can stress-test the new VRAM management and PBR textures on your own rigs.


​Thank you again for helping us build the ultimate anti-SaaS game dev tool. Let us know what you manage to break in this version!

replies.author: Blackie-Chan101
replies.body:
Hey there, 

Steam's strict trailer guidelines for utility software require us to show raw, continuous UI usage, which is why that first trailer is basically a 50-second timelapse of the generation log. But you're right, it's not a great viewing experience. We're working on cutting a punchier showcase video shortly with the new improved UI.

​Regarding the demo—there actually is a free demo live on the page right now! Steam sometimes hides the "Download Demo" button in a weird spot on the right-hand sidebar, so it's easy to miss. It runs the full V1.5 PyTorch pipeline so you can benchmark your GPU and see the actual texture outputs on your own rig.

​We know the price tag is an investment, which is exactly why we made the demo. Our entire goal was to offer a one-time, perpetual license so indie devs can escape those monthly $30/mo cloud AI subscriptions.

​Grab the demo, put your hardware through the wringer, and let us know what you think of the actual mesh outputs!

replies.author: Blackie-Chan101
replies.body:
You are 100% right—if you are rocking a 24GB RTX 3090 and know your way around Python dependencies, cloning the raw GitHub repo is an awesome way to go! It absolutely flies on that hardware.


​We built Jupetar for the devs who don't have 24GB of VRAM and don't want to mess with the command line.


​Running raw Hunyuan3D on a standard 10GB card (like an RTX 3080) usually results in an instant Out-Of-Memory crash. We spent weeks writing custom memory managers, VAE slicing, and VRAM offloading protocols so it gracefully runs on mid-range hardware.


​As for renting a cloud 4090—that's exactly what we wanted to escape! We wanted to sever the cloud umbilical cord completely. No hourly meters, no uploading proprietary concept art to remote servers. Just a perpetual, offline desktop app.


​Plus, Jupetar isn't just a wrapper. We baked in xAtlas for smart UV unwrapping, Real-ESRGAN for true 4K neural upscaling, and a custom glTF 2.0 ORM channel packer so the assets are actually game-ready for Unity/Unreal without looking like wet plastic.


​But yeah, if you've got a 3090 and love the terminal, you are definitely sitting in the absolute best-case scenario!
